proposal.description: run_counter keeps counting past max_on_counts and wraps instead of saturating at the ceiling
proposal.reason: If pwm_sync stays high, run_counter wraps to 0 after 2^ON_TIME_W - max_on_counts clocks. It then reads below the ceiling again, so pulse_allowed comes back on and pwm_out goes high again in the middle of the same stuck-high pulse.

proposal.description: The envelope is re-armed whenever the gated pulse ends, not only when pwm_sync goes low, so a truncated pulse re-arms while pwm_sync is still high
proposal.reason: When pwm_sync stays high for more than max_on_counts+1 clocks, pulse_allowed clears and the next clock takes the low-phase branch, which clears the counter and sets pulse_allowed again. pwm_out drops for one clock and then goes high again, giving the gate driver repeated pulses within one cycle.

proposal.description: The saturated-hold branch wins over the low-phase re-arm, so a counter at the ceiling is never cleared
proposal.reason: Once one pulse reaches the ceiling, run_counter stays at max_on_counts through the low phase and pulse_allowed stays 0. pwm_out then stays low for every later pulse until max_on_counts goes up.

proposal.description: The ceiling test is equality instead of less-than, so a ceiling lowered below the running count is missed
proposal.reason: If max_on_counts drops below run_counter while pwm_sync is high (soft_start resetting to the floor, or clamping to a lowered max_on_limit), the counter climbs on to wrap-around with pulse_allowed held at 1. pwm_out then follows pwm_sync far past the new ceiling.

proposal.description: pulse_allowed is decided from the post-increment count instead of the pre-edge run_counter, which removes the documented +1 clk offset
proposal.reason: For any max_on_counts of 1 or more, a pulse longer than the ceiling is cut after max_on_counts clocks instead of max_on_counts+1, so pwm_out's enforced on-time is one clock short.

proposal.description: The envelope is re-armed only once run_counter has already been cleared, one clock into the low phase, not on its first clock
proposal.reason: On the first low clock after a pulse, pulse_allowed goes to 0 while run_counter is still nonzero. If the low phase lasts only one clock (high duty), the next pulse starts with the gate closed, and pwm_out loses that pulse's first clock.
